title: Escape Diverges, Survival Coincides: (2,2) Is the Unique Preservation Survivor at the Abel–Ruffini Boundary
description: The parent file proved an ASYMMETRY of escape cost: starting from the solvable range {0,1,2,3,4}, the disjoint union first manufactures an unsolvable degree at 5 = 2 + 3, while the product must wait until 6 = 2 · 3 (5 is prime, hence multiplicatively unreachable). This entry examines the opposite face — PRESERVATION — and finds the reverse pattern: the two operations agree exactly. For NONTRIVIAL solvable pieces (each with ≥ 2 points), the composite stays solvable in one single case, the same for both operations. Perm (α ⊕ β) is solvable with card α, card β ≥ 2 iff card α = card β = 2 (perm_sum_nontrivial_solvable_iff): any larger summand pushes the sum to ≥ 5. Perm (α × β) is solvable with card α, card β ≥ 2 iff card α = card β = 2 (perm_prod_nontrivial_solvable_iff): any larger factor pushes the product to ≥ 6. So although ⊕ and × escape the solvable range at different degrees, their sets of surviving nontrivial pairs are IDENTICAL — the single pair (2,2) — and for nontrivial solvable pieces solvability of the sum-composite is equivalent to solvability of the product-composite (sum_prod_survival_coincide). Because 2 + 2 = 4 = 2 · 2, both composites land on the same degree 4 — the largest solvable symmetric degree (S₄ is solvable), one step below the threshold 5 (survivor_at_four, survivor_degree_below_threshold). The closing escape_diverges_survival_coincides sets the parent's asymmetry of escape beside this file's coincidence of survival.

overview.historicalContext: Abel–Ruffini rests on S₅ being non-solvable; classically Sₙ and Aₙ are solvable exactly for n ≤ 4. The parent chain read that threshold through the two monoidal structures on finite types — disjoint union (which adds point counts) and Cartesian product (which multiplies them) — and isolated an asymmetry of ESCAPE: the least degree pushed out of {0,1,2,3,4} from solvable inputs is 5 under ⊕ but 6 under ×, because 5 is prime and so multiplicatively unreachable. That asymmetry concerns where the solvable range first BREAKS. The dual question is where it HOLDS: which pairs of solvable pieces still produce a solvable composite. For trivial pieces (0 or 1 points) the composite reduces to the other piece, so the substantive question is for nontrivial pieces, those with at least 2 points — equivalently the solvable pieces of cardinality 2, 3, or 4.
overview.modernSignificance: Reading Perm as a functor on finite types, solvability of Perm (α ⊕ β) and Perm (α × β) is governed by card α + card β and card α · card β against the cap 4. For nontrivial pieces both constraints collapse to the same survivor: card α = card β = 2. Under ⊕ this is the linear fact that 2 + 2 = 4 but 2 + 3 = 5 already escapes; under × it is the nonlinear fact that 2 · 2 = 4 but 2 · 3 = 6 escapes — yet the surviving pair is the same. So the preservation side is SYMMETRIC where the escape side was asymmetric: solvability of the sum-composite is equivalent to solvability of the product-composite for nontrivial solvable pieces (sum_prod_survival_coincide), both occurring exactly on (2,2). The coincidence 2 + 2 = 2 · 2 sends both survivors to the single degree 4 = card (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) = card (Fin 2 × Fin 2), the largest solvable symmetric degree and the last rung below the Abel–Ruffini threshold.

meta.author: Classical (Sₙ/Aₙ solvable iff n ≤ 4); unique-survivor and survival-coincidence formalization original

mathlibDependencies.description: Fintype.card (α ⊕ β) = Fintype.card α + Fintype.card β. Behind perm_sum_solvable_iff, turns the union threshold into the linear constraint card α + card β ≤ 4 that the unique additive survivor solves.
Fintype.card (α × β) = Fintype.card α * Fintype.card β. Behind perm_prod_solvable_iff, turns the product threshold into card α · card β ≤ 4, the nonlinear constraint forcing both factors to 2.
a ≤ b ∧ c ≤ d ⟹ a * c ≤ b * d. With a factor ≥ 3 and the other ≥ 2 yields ≥ 6 > 4, the engine forcing the unique multiplicative survivor to be (2,2) (perm_prod_nontrivial_solvable_iff).
Fintype.card (Fin n) = n. Evaluates the concrete survivor Perm (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) and Perm (Fin 2 × Fin 2) at 4 points (survivor_at_four, survivor_degree_below_threshold).

originalContributions: card_nontrivial_solvable_mem: every nontrivial solvable piece has cardinality 2, 3, or 4 — the intrinsic cap card ≤ 4 with the degenerate 0/1 cases removed by the ≥ 2 hypothesis
perm_sum_nontrivial_solvable_iff: the UNIQUE additive survivor — for summands with ≥ 2 points each, Perm (α ⊕ β) is solvable iff both have exactly 2 points (2 + 2 = 4, while 2 + 3 = 5 escapes)

perm_prod_nontrivial_solvable_iff: the UNIQUE multiplicative survivor — for factors with ≥ 2 points each, Perm (α × β) is solvable iff both have exactly 2 points (the nonlinear cap forced factor-by-factor via Nat.mul_le_mul)

sum_prod_survival_coincide: survival coincides though escape diverges — for nontrivial solvable pieces, Perm (α ⊕ β) is solvable iff Perm (α × β) is, the preservation-side counterpart to the parent's escape-cost asymmetry

unique_survivor_characterization: either composite being solvable is equivalent to card α = card β = 2, and that condition makes both composites solvable — the survivor is unique up to both operations at once

survivor_at_four: the concrete survivor — Perm (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) and Perm (Fin 2 × Fin 2) are both solvable and 2 + 2 = 4 = 2 · 2, realising S₄ simultaneously as a sum and a product of two 2-point systems

survivor_degree_below_threshold: the surviving composite has 4 points and 4 + 1 = 5 reaches the unsolvable Perm (Fin 5) — the unique survivor sits at the very top of the solvable range, immediately below the Abel–Ruffini degree

escape_diverges_survival_coincides: the two faces side by side — the escape costs diverge (least nontrivial additive escape 5 < least multiplicative escape 6) while the survival is symmetric (sum-solvable iff product-solvable for nontrivial solvable pieces, both on (2,2))

mainTheorems.name: escape_diverges_survival_coincides
mainTheorems.statement: Escape: there is a nontrivial additive escape at 5 (= 2 + 3, both ≤ 4) but no product of two factors ≥ 2 equals 5, so the least nontrivial multiplicative escape is 6 > 5. Survival: for nontrivial solvable pieces, Perm (α ⊕ β) is solvable iff Perm (α × β) is, both occurring exactly on the unique pair (2,2) with 2 + 2 = 4 = 2 · 2.
mainTheorems.significance: Pairs the two faces of the Abel–Ruffini boundary {≤4} under the algebra of finite types. Where the range first BREAKS depends on the operation — additive degree 5, multiplicative degree 6 — but where it HOLDS does not: both ⊕ and × preserve solvability of nontrivial pieces only on the single pair (2,2), landing on the same degree 4 = S₄, the last solvable rung below the threshold.
